summary:
Round-3 fixes for core, runner and docs are done. I rebuilt everything from the repository root, and every suite I ran passed. That excludes two runner test files the safety rules forbid me to run (see open issues).

(1) MAJOR, the seed race, fixed. A new module, packages/runner/src/shadow/seed.ts, handles copying the user's .lake/build into a run's working copy, and createRunShadow now uses it:
- Listing the user's build, creating the run directory and copying the build all happen inside semantic.runExclusive, the same lock the board's in-place refresh holds.
- The copy is used only when it is a snapshot of a finished build:
  - no Lake build lock (lake.lock) is present;
  - no temporary file younger than 10 minutes (*.tmp or *.tmp.*) is present; older ones are leftovers of a crashed build and are skipped, not copied;
  - no compiled file is newer than its trace file. I checked in the Lake 4.35 sources, and with a real build, that Lake deletes a module's outputs before rebuilding it and writes the trace last;
  - every file keeps the same device, inode, size, mtime and ctime from the first listing, through its copy, to a second listing taken after the copy, and no file appears or disappears.
- Otherwise nothing is seeded and the run's first Lean job is a full build. The shadow's new optional `buildSeed` field says why, and the RunManager logs it. ENOENT no longer refuses a start, Lake's temporary files are never copied, and two builds are never mixed. A symlink or special file in .lake/build still refuses the shadow, as before.
- New test file packages/runner/test/shadow/seed.test.ts (8 tests): files replaced or removed between listing and copy, a file rewritten or added during the copy, an artifact newer than its trace, temporary files, the lock, waiting for a running runExclusive job, the verifier's race probe (one run: 5 skipped because a temporary file was being written, 1 because a file changed during the copy; never refused), and a real Lean refresh followed by a full seed.

(2) Examples, fixed (core rules.ts, describe.ts, types and index docs). Every `example` added since B, compared by text as a multiset so the user's own stay theirs, is now a finding in every purpose:
- before the round's freeze: `proof-before-freeze` with token `example`, now also in gate-other and gate-proved;
- after the freeze: `footprint` with token `example`, which has its own board sentence.
New core tests in rules.test.ts and describe.test.ts. A new end-to-end cheat script, test-fixtures/walkthrough/cheat-example-not-proved.json, replays the verifier's probe X-14 in walkthrough.e2e.test.ts: two retries, and Accept writes no example. Updated decisions-log 28 (a pointer to section 29), the new decisions-log section 29, user guide 10.6, and plan 3.3 and 10.3.

(3) System prompt, fixed. The rule sentence now says that everything Claude adds, including definitions, instances and structure fields, may rest only on the selected premises, and `example` is added to the forbidden list. Updated in systemPrompt.ts, the test fixture and plan 5.1; logged in plan section 14.

(4) Text coupling, fixed on my side. Core `RunView.accepted?: { changedFiles: boolean }` is set by the runner's Accept before the run ends and is saved in run.json; manager.accept.test.ts checks it. The webview's dependency on the notice wording is logged in plan section 14. Switching the webview to the new field is for the webview fixer.

(5) The two script tests: not run, as the safety rules forbid; the main session should run them.

(6) Raw diff placement: left open for the user, as the issue says.

Known limit of the seed checks: the artifact-newer-than-trace rule follows Lake 4.35's write order and the default lib/lean and ir directories. A package with a custom leanLibDir or irDir gets only the comparison within the trace's own directory, but the stability, temporary-file and lock checks still apply. A Lean job outside telelean that writes nothing for the whole copy window while a module is half rebuilt is caught only by that trace-order rule. A false positive only skips the seed, which costs a full build and never gives a wrong verdict.

Not run by me: the extension's VS Code smoke and e2e tests, and the webview's Playwright e2e tests. The main session should rerun them after both fixers finish, together with the full runner and core suites.

minor_decisions.decision: The new behaviour stays inside createRunShadow: it takes semantic.runExclusive itself when copyBuild is on. No new option was added for callers, and the RunManager is unchanged apart from a log line.
minor_decisions.rationale: There is a single caller (RunManager.start), it never runs inside a runExclusive job, and the extension bundles one copy of semantic/index, so the lock is shared with the board's refresh. Plan section 14 warns never to call it from inside a runExclusive job (that would deadlock).

minor_decisions.decision: Any doubt about the seed (a change, ENOENT, an unreadable build, a lock, a fresh temporary file, an artifact newer than its trace) seeds nothing. Only symlinks and special files still refuse the start.
minor_decisions.rationale: The issue asks to fall back, never refuse: an empty build is always correct, only slower (about a second for Spyro). The D-24 symlink refusal is a safety rule, not a race, so it stays.

minor_decisions.decision: A temporary file counts as 'a build is running' only if it is younger than 10 minutes; older ones are leftovers of a crashed build, skipped and not copied. lake.lock skips the seed at any age and is never copied.
minor_decisions.rationale: Lean writes an .olean under a temporary name only for an instant, so an old one is debris; without the age limit a crashed build would disable seeding for good. Lake 4.35 takes no build lock, but a copied lock from an older Lake would stall the working copy's Lake indefinitely.

minor_decisions.decision: Added a trace-order rule (no module artifact newer than its .trace) on top of the size and mtime re-check the issue suggested.
minor_decisions.rationale: Lake 4.35 writes a module's trace only after all its outputs. A snapshot taken while an outside Lake build sits between writing an .olean and writing its trace would pass the re-check and could make Lake trust an .olean built from other sources. Checked against the Lake 4.35 source and the mtimes of a real build (outputs, then hashes, then trace).

minor_decisions.decision: Examples are compared with B (the user's files at the run's start, or at Accept), not with the round's start, and are refused in every purpose. After the freeze they reuse the existing code `footprint` with token `example`; no new GateFindingCode was added.
minor_decisions.rationale: With this rule no passing state can contain a new example, so comparing with B is simpler and strictly stronger. Adding a member to GateFindingCode could break exhaustive switches in packages outside my paths; the webview labels findings by step (G3, 'what it rests on'), so the token alone is enough.

minor_decisions.decision: check_lean reports examples too, not only finish.
minor_decisions.rationale: Claude learns about an example at a check, which costs none of its 3 gate attempts. The system prompt also forbids examples up front.
